newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Indonesia to tender Natuna development project.
newsitem.headline: Indonesia to tender Natuna development project.

text.p: Indonesia will tender contracts early next month to develop the main Natuna island, astride the giant Natuna gas field, the Jakarta Post said on Wednesday.

Minister for Research and Technology Jusuf Habibie said tenders for the development of Natuna, the largest among a string of islands about 1,100 km (680 miles) north of Jakarta, would be accepted on October 1.
Habibie said the government was looking into the development of the island's transport system, water resources and public facilities but did not elaborate on the nature of contracts to be tendered.

In 1994, Indonesia signed a multibillion dollar deal with U.S.-based Exxon Corp to exploit the Natuna gas field around the islands, which contains an estimated 210 trillion cubic feet (tcf) of gas. Only 45 tcf are thought to be recoverable.
Indonesia's state-owned oil company Pertamina owns 24 percent of the Natuna project, Mobil Corp 26 percent and Exxon 50 percent. Gas from the field is expected to start flowing by 2003/4.
Indonesia is the world's largest producer of liquefied natural gas.
